subject: Collaborative roadshow + 'Inference at the Edge' webinar — partnership plan and calendar sync
messages:
From: Eileen Cho <eileen@eventspring.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: partners@eventspring.com, rajiv@edgeinference.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Joint roadshow + webinar idea — 'Inference at the Edge'

Hi Olga,

Hope you're well — I'm Eileen from EventSpring (we run partner roadshows and regional tech showcases). We loved Redwood's recent latency benchmarks and wanted to float an idea: partner on a small roadshow across three hubs (SF, Austin, London) this fall, anchored by a joint webinar titled "Inference at the Edge: cost & reliability tradeoffs."

High-level ask: would Redwood be open to co-hosting the webinar (30–40m + panel) and sharing booth space at the local meetups? We typically offer MDF for travel + a shared lead pool if both sides promote equally.

If this sounds interesting, can you share who on your side should be involved (marketing, partnerships, sales) and a rough availability window (Sept–Nov)? I can follow up with a one-page partnership brief and example MDF terms.

Thanks,
Eileen
Eileen Cho
Head of Partnerships, EventSpring
eileen@eventspring.com
(415) 555-0189

Attachment: EventSpring_Partner_Brief.pdf (one-page stub)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Eileen Cho <eileen@eventspring.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Joint roadshow + webinar idea — 'Inference at the Edge'

Hi Eileen — thanks for the note, this is right in our wheelhouse.

Quick answers: please loop in our field marketing lead Marissa (cc'd) and partnerships lead Vivek (cc'd). Sales (for opportunity tracking) is Lauren Bishop — I'll pull her in if we get past the ID stage.

Availability: short list of windows that work for us:
- Webinar: prefer mid-September week of 9/13 or late October week of 10/25 (avoiding major vendor conferences).
- Roadshow: 3-city rotation Sep 20–Oct 8 OR Oct 18–Nov 5. We can be flexible on order, but would like a 2-week lead time per city for logistics.

Key asks up front so we don't waste time:
- MDF: ballpark numbers for travel + co-marketing per city (we typically look for 6–8k USD per city for joint events).
- Booth: expected footprint and staffing needs (we usually send 2 SDRs + 1 solutions engineer).
- Lead share rules and MQL definitions (we need a clear SLA on lead handoffs).

If you can send the one-pager plus sample MDF terms, I'll circulate internally (Marissa to confirm ops details).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships (Americas) | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

--
Olga Petrov
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Joint roadshow + webinar idea — 'Inference at the Edge'

Thanks, Olga — attaching a draft MDF and partnership brief for your review.

Summary:
- MDF per city: $7,500 (covers local venue, basic AV, and 2 lead-capture passes).
- Marketing match: we ask partners to commit to a minimum of 3 co-marketing activities (email blast, social campaign, and 1 promoted post).
- Lead pool: EventSpring qualifies leads to a Tech Interest MQL; we share CSV weekly.
- Booth footprint: 10x10 with an option to expand to 10x20 at an added cost.

I've also included a suggested rotation order (SF -> Austin -> London) and a sample webinar agenda.

Attachment: CoMarketing_Terms_v1.pdf (draft MDF and deliverables)

Looking forward to Marissa's ops input — happy to hop on a quick sync this week.

Best,
Eileen

Folks — forwarding the draft MDF from EventSpring. Quick thoughts:

- MDF ask at $7.5k/city is within range but prefer splitting to $5k Redwood / $2.5k EventSpring per city if they can commit to paid social. That reduces our net spend and keeps incentive aligned.
- Booth: SF we can commit to 10x20; Austin probably 10x10; London TBD (need budget approval).
- Staffing: agree on 2 SDRs + 1 SE per US city; propose rotating Redwood AE/SE in London to support follow-ups.
- Lead handing: we need clear SLA — propose 72-hour lead delivery into HubSpot and AE outreach within 48 hours of handoff.

Marissa — can you confirm ops lead time for booth gear and a rough estimate for shipping costs SF vs London?
Lauren — if this looks like a viable expansion/opportunity, can you spin up a HubSpot opp (I can share the EventSpring brief) and mark quadrant as 'Co-Marketing — Roadshow'?

If we can agree on MDF split and SLAs, I'll send a counterproposal back to Eileen.

Thanks,
Olga

Eileen — thanks for the draft and for the quick turnaround. We discussed internally and can proceed with the following agreement:

1) MDF split: Redwood commits $5,000 per city; EventSpring commits $2,500 per city plus a paid social push (minimum $1,000 ad spend) on their channels.
2) Booth allocation: SF 10x20 (Redwood covers additional booth bump fees), Austin 10x10, London 10x10 (Redwood to request travel budget).
3) Staffing & rotation: Redwood will send 2 SDRs + 1 SE for each US city; LAE/AE rotation for London.
4) Lead SLAs: EventSpring provides weekly CSV export; Redwood agrees to 72-hour MQL ingestion into HubSpot and 48-hour AE outreach.
5) Webinar: target webinar week of 9/13 (we'll lock final date once both comms plans are approved).
